lines: {target}? Black stone and lava leave little mercy. I would count everyone twice.
If anyone heads for Basalt Deltas, tell them: Step like every block wants an argument. I will be at the loom.
Ash and basalt make the Nether feel broken twice. I'll remember that when I count everyone.
Basalt Deltas is no small story. Fear scatters folk like a loose flock.
I will remember Basalt Deltas as as jagged black country with heat in its cracks. I will count heads before I count sheep.
{target}? I would not rush toward it without telling someone where you are going first.
That kind of place makes a simple walk feel like a decision. Pack food, count your torches, and keep your head clear.
I have heard enough about {target} to know the quiet parts are usually the ones to worry about.
If you go there, come back with the story and not just the scratches. The village remembers both.
A place like {target} can turn confidence into <shake>panic</shake> very quickly.
